title: Palace: No agreed terms, timeline yet for PH-US trade deal
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has yet to agree on the terms of the trade deal announced by United States President Donald Trump during his state visit to the Philippines, Malacañang said on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published November 24, 2026 3:52pm
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has yet to agree on the terms of the trade deal announced by United States President Donald Trump during his state visit to the Philippines, Malacañang said on Tuesday.
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said the two countries had yet to finalize the agreement, including its timeline.
"Wala pang terms (There are no terms that the President has agreed to yet)” Castro said in a press briefing.
"Pinag-usapan lang po ay bilisan kung ano man transaction na maaaring mangyari, bilisan ang pagkatrabaho mula sa representative ng Pilipinas at sa representative ng US," she added.
(The discussion was only about expediting any transactions that may take place and speeding up the work between Philippine and US representatives.)
Trump earlier announced that the Philippines would import 100% of its agricultural products and energy requirements from the US starting Jan. 1 next year.
However, Castro said there was no definite timeline for the trade deal as Cabinet members had yet to submit their recommendations.
She explained that the agreement would give the Philippines the option to source commodities from other suppliers.
"Ang lahat po na gagawin na transaction ay makakabuti, kung di man makakabuti pareho sa dalawang bansa, makakabuti ito dapat sa Pilipinas," Castro said.
(Every transaction that will be made should be beneficial. If it is not beneficial to both countries, it should at least benefit the Philippines.)
Castro said the Philippines would remain free to choose its suppliers based on what would be most beneficial to the country.

"Depende sa situasyon. Kung saan mas makakabuti sa bansa natin, yun po ang gagawin ng Pangulo. Halimbawa yung dati nating pinagkukunan ng source, mas mataas o hindi na available o mahirap pasukin, talagang maghahanap ang Pangulo ng bagong source," she added.

(It depends on the situation. The President will choose whatever is best for the Philippines. For example, if our previous source is more expensive, no longer available or difficult to access, the President will look for a new source.)

In a media briefing following the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, Marcos clarified Trump's claim that the Philippines had agreed to source all its agricultural and energy supplies exclusively from the US.
Marcos said the Philippines instead wanted to diversify its sources of basic commodities, which was why it had opened its markets to the US.

“The way I put it is that if you are standing on one foot, sa isa ka lang umaasa, madaling magka problema (if you are relying on only one source, you can easily run into problems)," the President said.
"Kapag marami kang naaasahan, kahit magka problema ng isa, pwede ka pang tumakbo duon sa mga iba. And that's why the trade deal is important,” he added.
(If you have several sources to rely on, even if one encounters a problem, you can turn to the others. And that's why the trade deal is important.)— MCG, GMA News
